images.alt: Paulus stuurt Epafroditus terug — Filippenzen 2:28; tekstillustratie.
images.prompt: Use case: historical-scene. Photorealistic illustration of an explicit biblical comparison or event, first-century Roman Judea and Galilee, landscape 3:2, natural materials and daylight, anatomically coherent people with exactly two arms and animals with correct limbs; fully covering modest opaque robes. No modern objects, readable writing, portrait of God the Father, blood, injury or watermark. Philippians 2:25–30: Paul sends Epaphroditus back to the Philippian believers after the latter recovered from a nearly fatal illness. Exactly two adult men: Paul speaks warmly to a recovered but travel-weary Epaphroditus at the doorway of a simple first-century room. Epaphroditus has a small plain travel bag and is preparing to depart, not being shown dying or wounded. Modest opaque robes, natural two arms each, no modern medical equipment, no invented diagnosis or readable letter. Focus on affectionate sending and honouring a trusted coworker.

images.alt: Lesbeeld: Euodia en Syntyche helpen — Filippenzen 4:3; tekstillustratie.
images.prompt: Use case: historical-scene. Photorealistic illustration of an explicit biblical comparison or event, first-century Roman Judea and Galilee, landscape 3:2, natural materials and daylight, anatomically coherent people with exactly two arms and animals with correct limbs; fully covering modest opaque robes. No modern objects, readable writing, portrait of God the Father, blood, injury or watermark. Illustrate the appeal in Philippians 4:2–3: an unnamed trusted fellow worker helps two adult women Euodia and Syntyche toward agreement in the Lord. Two adult women sit facing each other with an adult helper nearby listening with open calm hands. Serious kind discussion in a modest first-century Philippian home, no fight, accusation, forced reconciliation or declaration that the problem was already resolved. Exactly three main adults, no readable labels, fully covering modest robes and coherent hands. The image is an illustrative response to Paul’s request, not a report of its historical outcome.
